To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) the ligands of CsPbBr 3 QDs can be modified by photochromic diarylethene ligands and (b) the photochromism can be used to control the luminescence of the QDs.

(i) we have synthesized a series of diarylethene ligands that are able to switch the luminescence of CsPbBr 3 nanocrystals; (ii) the switching efficiency is strongly dependent on the ligand’s structure and the ligand-to-pQD ratio; (iii) the switching mechanism involves a ligand exchange between the diarylethene and the pQD surface, as demonstrated by XPS, FT-IR, and UV-vis measurements;

the luminescence properties of CsPbBr 3 perovskite quantum dots can be reversibly switched on and off by the addition of photochromic diarylethene ligands, which are able to quench the emission by a photoinduced energy transfer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel organic-inorganic hybrid materials based on diarylethenes (DAE), which are a class of photochromic molecules, and perovskite nanocrystals (PNCs).
the synthesis, characterization and application of novel photochromic materials.
the development of new photochromic materials for applications in optoelectronics, such as optical switches, sensors, and displays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the luminescence properties of CsPbBr 3 NCs are strongly dependent on their shape, size and the presence or not of ligands, which can be tuned by controlling the synthetic conditions.
the luminescence properties of the CsPbBr 3 NCs are significantly improved by the introduction of the diarylethenes.
the luminescent properties of the colloidal CsPbX3 (X = Br, I) perovskite NCs are highly dependent on the surface ligands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the first example of luminescence photoswitching of colloidal perovskite QDs by photochromic diarylethene ligands.
we have developed a new class of luminescent colloidal CsPbX3 (X = Cl, Br, I) nanocrystals (NCs) by using photochromic diarylethene ligands as the surface ligands.
we have demonstrated the possibility to tune the emission color of CsPbBr 3 NCs by using photochromic diarylethene molecules as ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the luminescence of pQDs can be controlled in a reversible fashion by the use of photochromic ligands.
we can use photochromism in a new way to control the emission properties of pQDs.
we have demonstrated a new type of photoswitchable nanocrystals, where we can reversibly switch the emission color of colloidal pQDs by using photochromic diarylethene ligands.
